forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Internal audit reports delivery of the 2026/27 plan as On Track to timetable, with 134 total review and follow-up days.
news_drafts.lead: Fieldwork for the Council Tax and Members Expenses reviews was completed in the first week of November 2026, with draft reports in preparation. ToRs are agreed for Recruitment, Retention and Vetting, Campus Security, and Leisure Centres (Contract Management).
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report

news_drafts.headline: The Electoral Services review was replaced in the 2026/27 plan by Parking Services, with the paper citing pressures from the reinstated mayoral and district elections.
news_drafts.lead: The paper says Parking Services replaced Electoral Services in the plan. It then says Parking Services was itself replaced by the Utilities review, which is covered in the separate change noted above.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report

news_drafts.headline: The Utilities & Energy Management review was moved into the 2026/27 plan after receiving Limited assurance last year, because the required information was not provided on time.
news_drafts.lead: The S151 Officer approved the change, with the Utilities review replacing Parking Services in the plan. The paper says the review is a priority to be completed in this plan year, and it is scheduled for planning with a 4 January 2027 latest target.
news_drafts.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: Internal audit reports delivery of the 2026/27 plan as On Track to timetable, with 134 total review and follow-up days.
findings.detail: Fieldwork for the Council Tax and Members Expenses reviews was completed in the first week of November 2026, with draft reports in preparation. ToRs are agreed for Recruitment, Retention and Vetting, Campus Security, and Leisure Centres (Contract Management).
findings.matters: A finance director would see from this that the plan is on schedule, and that the pipeline of reviews through to March 2027 is set out with dates.
findings.quote: RAG status of delivery of the 2026/27 Plan to timetable On Track

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: The Electoral Services review was replaced in the 2026/27 plan by Parking Services, with the paper citing pressures from the reinstated mayoral and district elections.
findings.detail: The paper says Parking Services replaced Electoral Services in the plan. It then says Parking Services was itself replaced by the Utilities review, which is covered in the separate change noted above.
findings.matters: Councils planning audit coverage around a major election year may face the same trade-offs between internal audit and service pressures.
findings.quote: Parking Services had previously replaced Electoral Services in the Plan to reflect the significant pressures on the service this year from the reinstated mayoral and district elections.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A - Internal Audit Progress Report
findings.headline: The Utilities & Energy Management review was moved into the 2026/27 plan after receiving Limited assurance last year, because the required information was not provided on time.
findings.detail: The S151 Officer approved the change, with the Utilities review replacing Parking Services in the plan. The paper says the review is a priority to be completed in this plan year, and it is scheduled for planning with a 4 January 2027 latest target.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council would want to know that a weakness in timely information supply to internal audit led to a limited opinion and a re-prioritised review.
findings.quote: The Utilities review received a Limited assurance last year by Internal Audit as the required information was not provided on time.

findings.headline: Capital and specific reserves will be drawn down in later years, mostly for Simpler Recycling.
findings.detail: The notes say the reserves hold revenue contributions set aside in prior years. Their drawdown depends on the timing of specific project delivery.
findings.matters: A drawdown that depends on delivery timing can move again if the Simpler Recycling schedule slips, so a finance officer elsewhere would want to track it.
findings.quote: will be drawn down in subsequent years and relate mostly to Simpler Recycling.

findings.headline: The £22,026k programme is financed by £13,892k of grants and contributions, £6,134k of capital and specific reserves and £2,000k of capital receipts.
findings.detail: Table 3 shows the amounts drawn down to fund the programme. The notes say the reserves hold revenue contributions set aside in prior years and relate mostly to Simpler Recycling.
findings.matters: Reserves funding £6,134k of the programme shows how much of the capital plan depends on earlier revenue contributions being drawn down over time.
findings.figures: Total funding £22,026k; capital receipts £2,000k; grants/contributions/S106 £13,892k; capital and specific reserves £6,134k
